title: Example 17-2: Foreign Language Vocabulary List with Articles

illustrates.quote: Use the following format when articles, reflexive pronouns, special print signs, or specially marked items are shown before foreign language words in a vocabulary list. a. Begin the longest article...in cell 1. b. Align the initial letters of the foreign language words...

print.notes: Foreign words (with preceding Spanish articles la/las/el of varying length) in bold, translations in italic.
print.printFeatures: Two print columns (foreign phrase w/ article, translation); each entry's left margin in braille is driven by the block's own LONGEST article (17.7.3a), not a fixed indent.

braille.notes: Byte-identical between A and B; matches independent re-extraction exactly.

resolution: Both runs (A, B) came from the same model (Gemini Pro via Antigravity, 17 Sep 2026) and are not independent; agreement was treated as no evidence. braille.lines independently re-extracted from references/_text/braille-formats-2016.txt (the line-number field, digits + >=3 spaces, or the fixed left margin measured in ASCII spaces before any U+2800 cell, stripped by counting; U+2800->space; trailing spaces removed). Braille: A and B agree, matches source exactly (including the 1-space/0-space/4-space per-entry left-margin variation driven by article length). illustrates.rule: '17.7.3' (unchanged, both agreed) — the example sits directly after clause f, before §17.8 begins. Modeled as a 'glossary' block; expect a MISMATCH on the per-entry left margin, since glossarySegments/formatGlossary give every entry the SAME fixed margin from `level` alone, never from the block's own longest-article content length (17.7.3a-f) — F-212.
